questions.explanation: Emphatic 'do' + base verb stresses the truth of the statement against doubt.
options: I do apologise for the delay

questions.explanation: 'Did' + base verb adds strong emphasis contradicting a negative assumption.
questions.q: Contrary to rumours, she ___ the marathon.

questions.explanation: Emphatic 'do' works with imperatives to add urgency or politeness.
Repetition of the verb in a short answer adds emphatic confirmation.
The pro-verb 'do so' avoids repeating the full verb phrase emphatically.
questions.q: He promised to resign, and he did ___.

questions.explanation: Only the 'do' version emphatically contradicts the denial.
Emphatic 'do' can stress a habitual truth the listener doubts.
The emphatic negative uses 'do not' + base verb with stress on 'do'.
'Do' + base verb in the past emphatic form is 'did' + base, never 'did' + past.
questions.q: He ___ to the meeting after all.

questions.explanation: Repeating the adjective with 'and' intensifies it rhetorically.
The 'the more ... the more' correlative repeats the comparative for emphasis.
options: More the money, more the problems
The more money, the more problems
The money more, the problems more

questions.explanation: Emphatic 'do' stresses volition: 'I do want' contradicts 'you don't want'.
Reduplication ('again and again') is a rhetorical intensifier.
questions.q: He knocked ___, but no one answered.

questions.explanation: Only the emphatic 'do' version stresses the remembered fact.
The triple repetition builds rhetorical climax, a classic emphatic device.
options: I came, I saw, I conquered
I came and I saw and I conquered
questions.q: Choose the most rhetorically emphatic version.

questions.explanation: Emphatic 'did' + base contradicts the claim that nothing happened.
questions.q: Something ___ that night, whatever they say.

questions.explanation: The emphatic imperative 'do' + base verb softens a command into an earnest request.
Repeating the noun with 'after' expresses relentless succession.
Emphatic 'do' with 'have' stresses possession against doubt.
The doubled comparative 'more and more' marks gradual emphatic increase.
